supporting_observations.claim: At 13:39:57, WS-ICHEN-01 accepted a network logon for sam.okafor from WS-SOKAFOR-01. The subsequent PowerShell process used the same logon ID, 0x9ab2f6f.
At 13:42:01, sam.okafor ran PowerShell with the command line for the organization's documented workstation-patching script, \\FILE-NWD-01\Admin\Apply-Updates.ps1.
The PowerShell activity is consistent with the reported brief window: it started at 13:42:01 and ended at 13:42:47, close to the reported approximate time of 13:40 UTC.
During the patching activity, the proxy recorded a Windows Update download of about 38.8 MB; PowerShell had a connection to the proxy, and it launched wusa.exe to install a Windows update package.
The update installer and PowerShell process both exited shortly afterward; the available process records do not show a suspicious child process in this patching sequence.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection was unavailable on WS-NBLAKE-01 from 13:30 to 14:10 UTC, so activity on that host during that interval cannot be assessed from those sensors.
The records show the PowerShell command line and network activity, but do not include the contents or hash of Apply-Updates.ps1 or the installed MSU package.
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish the exact on-screen appearance or visibility of the PowerShell window.
The evidence does not independently verify the integrity or contents of the patch script or MSU package.
